title: Working at Height: The Basics
whatItIs: Work at height is work anywhere you could fall a distance liable to cause injury, even at or below ground level. It remains one of the biggest causes of deaths at work.

keyFacts.text: Work at height MUST be avoided where the job can reasonably be done safely another way.
Collective protection (eg guard rails) MUST come before personal protection (eg a harness).
Work at height MUST only go ahead when the weather doesn't put people's safety at risk.
You MUST report any activity or defect at height that you know is likely to endanger anyone.

keyFacts: HSG150: there's no distinction between low and high falls. Any work at height needs precautions.
If harnesses are used, plan how to rescue someone left hanging: don't rely on the emergency services.

visual.caption: Avoid, prevent, minimise: move on only when the step before isn't reasonably practicable

items.title: Avoid
items.text: Do as much as possible from the ground, eg with extending tools.

items.title: Prevent a fall
items.text: Existing safe place, then guarded scaffolds, towers or MEWPs, then work restraint.

items.title: Minimise the fall
items.text: Nets or air bags close under the work (collective) before a fall-arrest harness (personal).

a.label: Work restraint
points: Short lanyard stops you reaching the edge
Prevents the fall happening at all

b.label: Fall arrest
points: Minimises the distance and consequences of a fall
Needs a high anchor point and a rescue plan

onTheTest.question: You are planning a job at height. What must be considered first?
options: Which harness and lanyard to use
Whether the work can be done without working at height
Whether a net can go underneath
onTheTest.why: Work at Height Regs reg 6(2): don't work at height where the job can reasonably be done safely another way. Avoid comes first.

onTheTest.question: Which of these protects everyone on a platform, not just one person?
onTheTest.why: INDG401: a guard rail is collective protection and works without the worker acting. A harness is personal protection. Collective comes first (reg 7).

traps: There is no 'safe' low height: HSE draws no distinction between low and high falls.
A harness is not a first choice: picking it before options higher up the hierarchy isn't acceptable.
Ladders aren't banned, but they don't prevent a fall: use them only for low-risk, short jobs.
Falling into a hole in the ground counts as a fall from height too.
